extracted.intended_audience: mathematics students, instructors, and problem-solvers (including contest participants and anyone learning to write solutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Pólya's four-step heuristic for solving mathematical problems and writing solutions: understand the problem, devise a plan, carry out the plan, and look back, plus a list of heuristics for devising a plan and criteria for what makes a good solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify what is asked and what information is given; determine whether the conditions can be satisfied and whether they suffice to determine the unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: What is the unknown? What are the data? What is the condition? Is it possible to satisfy the condition? Is the condition sufficient to determine the unknown? Insufficient? Redundant? Contradictory? Draw a figure. Introduce suitable notation. Separate the various parts of the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devise a plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate a strategy to solve the problem, drawing on known problems and transformations of the current problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: Have you seen this problem before? In a slightly different form? Do you know a related problem? Could you use it? Could you restate the problem? More generally? More specifically? Analogously? If you cannot solve the problem, can you solve a related, easier problem? Part of the problem? A more general problem? A more special case? Did you use all the data? All the conditions?

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry out the plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute the chosen solution method carefully and verify each step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check each step: can you see clearly that the step is correct? Can you prove it is correct?

rubrics_metrics.name: Look back (review the solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine and reflect on the completed solution to check correctness and to extract further insight or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the solution. Can you check the result? Can you check the argument? Can you derive the result differently? Can you see it at a glance? Can you use the result, or the method, for some other problem?

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a similar problem whose solution might guide the current one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for problems already solved that resemble the current problem and adapt their methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve a more general problem of which the current problem is a special case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden the statement to reveal structure or enable known methods to apply; sometimes the general case is easier to reason about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Try small, extreme, or boundary cases to gain insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate particular cases, small values, extreme parameters, or simplified versions to detect patterns or counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Break the problem into sub-problems that are easier to solve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split the task into components, solve each piece, and combine the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recombination (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble pieces of known results to form a solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use known lemmas, theorems, or solved subproblems and combine them to reach the desired conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working backwards (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start from the desired conclusion and reason backwards toward the hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the conclusion and deduce necessary intermediate results that lead to known facts or the given data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary problem (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invent a related problem that is easier to solve and helps solve the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an auxiliary question whose solution provides insight or a stepping stone to the main problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary element (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a construction—an extra line in a figure or an extra variable—to facilitate the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce additional elements (constructions, variables) that make relationships clearer or enable standard techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary the problem (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relax or tighten conditions to explore variants that may be easier to solve or reveal structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust assumptions or parameters (make the problem easier or harder) to find fruitful perspectives or invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry (heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit or impose symmetry to simplify the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for symmetric structure or transform the problem to a symmetric setting to reduce complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how the result was found
rubrics_metrics.description: A good solution shows not only that the result is true but how it was discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose the reasoning and heuristic steps so the reader understands the discovery process, not only the polished final argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality of the method
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer methods that generalize to neighboring problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong solution presents techniques that apply to related problems, indicating broader utility beyond the single result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible 'Look back' step
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the solution has been reviewed: alternative approaches and context should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include checks, alternative derivations, or discussion of how the result fits with other knowledge; make the reflection evident in the exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposition mirrors discovery (avoid over-polishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer an account that reveals the discovery process rather than a fully-polished presentation that hides ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write solutions that mirror the thinker’s path—show key insights and near-misses—rather than presenting only a streamlined, opaque proof.
